I also get this error message when opening and closing various editor menus such as the settings menu:

ERROR: platform/linuxbsd/wayland/wayland_thread.cpp:1956 - Parameter "ws" is null.

Looking at that code, I can't say that this error message is related to the primary bug in this issue but I thought I should include it as a note.
Fixed...

I can confirm changing window size doesn't work on Linux since updating to 4.6 stable.
It zooms in/out depending on if you set a bigger/smaller window size, it's weird.

Confirming the issue as posted by OP also occurs on PopOS with COSMIC desktop (Wayland). Reproducing on 4.6 and 4.6.1 RC2. The issue happens when the "Embed Game" feature is enabled (e.g. through "Embedding Options"), and the problem is not that the game is running at a lower resolution (it might, but only if you have a Stretch mode enabled), but that the window size itself is much smaller than the viewport sizes specified in Project Settings. For e.g.: You can see that the window is not properly sized, does not fit the full game area, and nor is the window position respected (my project specifies `initial_position_type` to "Center of Primary Screen"). Again, this only happens when the "embed" feature is enabled on Wayland. Interestingly, however, if the "embed" feature is not enabled, the run window is sized properly, but it seems Godot opens it in XWayland mode. I believe this to be the case because I can use xprop to query the window information. For example, I get the following info from the non-embedded window: ``` xprop ERROR: Parameter "ws" is null. at: _wl_pointer_on_frame (platform/linuxbsd/wayland/wayland_thread.cpp:1956) Godot Engine v4.6.stable.official.89cea1439 - https://godotengine.org WARNING: XCreateIC couldn't create wd.xic. at: _create_xic (platform/linuxbsd/x11/display_server_x11.cpp:6330) Vulkan 1.4.311 - Forward Mobile - Using Device #0: AMD - AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV RENOIR) _NET_WM_ICON(CARDINAL) = Icon (128 x 128): (not shown) _NET_WM_NAME(UTF8_STRING) = "PhysicsTest (DEBUG)" _VARIABLE_REFRESH(CARDINAL) = 1 WM_STATE(WM_STATE): window state: Normal icon window: 0x0 _MOTIF_WM_HINTS(_MOTIF_WM_HINTS) = 0x3, 0x3e, 0x7e, 0x0, 0x0 _NET_WM_STATE(ATOM) = _NET_WM_STATE_FOCUSED WM_NORMAL_HINTS(WM_SIZE_HINTS): program specified location: 3840, 960 program specified size: 1152 by 648 program specified minimum size: 64 by 64 program specified maximum size: 16384 by 16384 window gravity: Static _NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE(ATOM) = _NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE_NORMAL WM_CLASS(STRING) = "Godot_Engine", "PhysicsTest" XdndAware(ATOM) = BITMAP WM_PROTOCOLS(ATOM): protocols WM_DELETE_WINDOW WM_NAME(STRING) = "PhysicsTest (DEBUG)" _NET_WM_PID(CARDINAL) = 1025194 ``` When running the game with the embed feature enabled, xprop won't query the run window at all. Another interesting thing was that when I changed the Viewport Mode to "Maximized", it reverts to the non-embedded XWayland window, **even if I have "Embed Game on Next Play" enabled in Embedding Options**. And in this case, instead of the window being maximized, it is sized as per viewport size specified in project settings. NOTE: The above XWayland windows appear when the display server driver is set to "default" in project settings (even if "Prefer Wayland" is already set in the editor settings). If you explicitly change the display server driver in project settings to "wayland", then xprop no longer queries the window, and **if you have embedding DISABLED** the window will be sized according to the viewport size. If you have embedding enabled, the issue with the small window size persists.
Hi, thank you for the reports! Can you replicate this with the embedded game _not_ in a floating window? See:

> Hi, thank you for the reports! Can you replicate this with the embedded game _not_ in a floating window?

It does not happen if game workspace is not floating. The game opens within the main editor window itself and is stretched or sized correctly per the settings.

This fixed the issue in 4.6.1..
(Debian trixie, Wayland RX6600)

The problem on my end is that the Project Setting "Window/**Resizeable** - Unchecked" was ignored..

So the app ran in a Smaller window, and the base Resolution was not respected being stretched down.

-Now when trying the options:
"Embed Game on Next Play"
"Make workspace Floating on Next Play"

One option made the app be embedded inside Godot Editor itself, which is not what I needed.

The other option Fixed the problem, 
and now my app runs on a floating borderless Full Resolution window,
respecting the resolution set in Project Settings, and the Resizable option, just as expected.

I did some more tests, and I could not replicate this in either GNOME nor KWin. For some reason, the window seems to *start* small. Like, requested by the engine. I have no idea why this seems to happen only on COSMIC.

> The problem on my end is that the Project Setting "Window/Resizeable" was ignored..

Do you mean that you can't resize the window manually?

-The only problem left in my case now is:
The borderless Full Res window can be placed anywhere on the screen, almost...

It can be placed in a spot where it extends beyond the Right, Left or Bottom limits of the screen. < Perfect!

It cannot be placed where it extends beyond the TOP limit of the screen. < Problem

That means I cannot see the bottom end of the app, and press the Menu button,
and thus interact normally with the app.

-In 4.5 and earlier versions that was not a problem,
and so I could run the app full res, and place the window wherever I needed it to be...

That's positive because I could see the app in full pixel-perfect resolution.

Now the only option will be rotating the monitor 90º, 
which is doable (Asus Proart), albeit not ideal..

-I guess the new Top Limit is something Wayland related?

> 
> Do you mean that you can't resize the window manually?

All the contrary!

Now when then Resizable option is checked > The window can be manually resized to Any size, 
Smaller size but also Bigger size than the base resolution in Project Settings.

-Toying with the options:
"Embed Game on Next Play"
"Make workspace Floating on Next Play"

Helped me fix the issue, and now the "Resizable" setting is respected!

(Before it was not being respected, and the window was Smaller, yet Fully Resizable!)

-The only problem left in my case will be the Top Limit one..

But yeah all this seems something Wayland related, which makes it harder to tackle, 
as each distro may be on a different point of wayland integration..

In any case this is the situation on a fully updated Debian trixie, 
runing Plasma/Wayland on an AMD RX6600.

> I did some more tests, and I could not replicate this in either GNOME nor KWin. For some reason, the window seems to _start_ small. Like, requested by the engine. I have no idea why this seems to happen only on COSMIC.

Yeah, it seems @AddisonH was also running COSMIC (PopOS 24.04). It sounds like @ernzo's problem is something a little different than what the OP and I are experiencing, and they are on Plasma. In my case there was never any issue with resizing the window, just that the initial size was too small.

Any idea how to proceed?

Since we're at it..
Does the Window/**Resizable** option have any effect when Exporting to Android as I'm assuming?

I can see the "Note: this setting is ignored on IOS",
but what about the rest of platforms?

Maybe it will make sense to have the Editor setting, and the Export setting Separated.. right?
as this can lead to confusion..

For instance,
I need to Edit the app in Full Res - Resizable Unchecked;
But I need to export to Android so when exporting -> Resizable Checked!

It's a small detail that can be easily overlooked, and I imagine could be an actual problem..

But yeah, given the structure of godot engine, shared by editor/template, 
it may not be that straightforward to decouple?

I took a look at the cosmic-epoch issue that you created and I have also experienced that variation of the problem where the viewport itself disconnected from the run window frame. I had that issue in Godot 4.5 and solved it by ticking the "Prefer Wayland" setting in Platform settings. Now in 4.6 I get this new problem with the window size. Occasionally I still do get that embedded viewport disconnection bug but it is inconsistent.

A game I've exported to Android has the resizable option turned on, and it works on desktop as expected but it has no effect on Android. You can't resize the window in any way (that I know of) on the phone.

Welp, I was writing a big message and stuff with my ideas when I had a hunch and had to check it.

Looks like I found the issue! Apparently COSMIC reported *all* output modes (which is fine, albeit deprecated) and I did not take into account that this was a thing. Basically, Godot thought your display was the smallest resolution your GPU supported. Take that, plus the fact that window restoring is temporarily disabled (see #113656), and it always tried to center the window in a tiiiny screen, scrunching the poor thing to the minimum possible.

PR incoming!
Hi, PR #116236 is up. Please give it a spin :D
Awesome. I'll try it out when I get a chance to set up building Godot from source (which I haven't done before), hopefully soon.

Just tried the fix and it's definitely a huge improvement! The window is no longer squished. However, still not entirely correct: 1. The window is now much larger, but it doesn't exactly match the game size. It's wider (see first screenshot below), and for portrait style games it seems it does not cover the full height of the game (see screenshots 2 & 3) ^^ The window has opened wider that the game's actual width (as shown by the red arrows) ^^ The first image in the series above is the original height that the window opened at, and you can see from the second image that the actual game height is greater than that. 2. The second issue is that the window position is not being respected. The window opens slightly to the right of the screen instead of centered. This isn't such a bother for me, but just thought I'd mention.

> Just tried the fix and it's definitely a huge improvement! The window is no longer squished.

Awesome! Thank you for testing!

> 1. The window is now much larger, but it doesn't exactly match the game size. It's wider (see first screenshot below), and for portrait style games it seems it does not cover the full height of the game (see screenshots 2 & 3)

That seems to be related to the fact that, since window restoring is disabled, it (more or less????) chooses the default quarter-of-the-(first)-screen size. I'll experiment with disabling that fallback too and see if it's possible to improve the situation without breaking other stuff.

> 2. The second issue is that the window position is not being respected. The window opens slightly to the right of the screen instead of centered. This isn't such a bother for me, but just thought I'd mention.

That's weird, we have absolutely no control over the window's position on the screen. Perhaps it gets resized half-way and COSMIC does not compensate for that? No idea.

Hi. @riverfr0zen could you please give a shot at my [wl/restore-workaround](https://github.com/deralmas/godot/tree/wl/restore-workaround) branch? It hopefully implements a better workaround for the window HiDPI bug.
Update: if anybody tried it please be aware that I pused a fix, the scale was truncated to an int due to an implicit cast.

> Hi. [@riverfr0zen](https://github.com/riverfr0zen) could you please give a shot at my [wl/restore-workaround](https://github.com/deralmas/godot/tree/wl/restore-workaround) branch? It hopefully implements a better workaround for the window HiDPI bug. I applied your changes and it works really well! There are some notes: When running the first time after opening a project, the window size is now large enough to cover the whole game, but the game itself seems to run at a smaller resolution: If you close the game window and run again, all the subsequent runs open the window and game at the matching size, as would be expected: All in all it's a great fix and the issue at the beginning is quite negligible. EDIT: Actually I just noticed, as you can see from the sizes indicated on the screenshots, it seems the first time it opens up, the window is *slightly* shorter than the viewport size settings, which is why the game itself scaled down (I have integer scaling enabled on this game).

Thank you for testing! I did a quick investigation and could not get to anything conclusive on why this happens. I also noticed that the results seem to differ on COSMIC when compared with plasma (in a VM) or labwc (natively) so maybe it's limited to there.

I'll begin making a PR with this fix, hopefully this will get sorted out while polishing the rest, there's still lots to do.
Yeah, the fix so far is already a vast improvement. Thanks so much for looking into it!
Is the #116308 pull request also going to be merged? Because it completes this issue imo.
